headline: Laid-off H-1B visa holder successfully switches career to 'professional stationary object' to avoid immediate deportation
body: After learning that the 60-day grace period for unemployed visa holders has been revoked, a former software engineer has permanently anchored himself to a park bench in Palo Alto to qualify as a piece of city infrastructure. By effectively transitioning into a 'municipal fixture,' he claims he is no longer an employee subject to labor laws, but rather a permanent civic installation that technically doesn't require a work permit to exist.
caption: Living life as a park bench is definitely one way to handle the new visa rules. Would you choose wood or iron? #H1B #WorkVisa #ImmigrationNews #Satire (satire)
igHook: Would you rather be a park bench or a mailbox if it meant you could stay in the country?
imagePrompt: A wide-angle, slightly blurry shot of an empty wooden park bench situated on a quiet, tree-lined sidewalk in an urban tech hub, captured during the golden hour.

sourceHeadline.title: H-1B visa holders won't get 60-day grace period after job loss as Trump administration revises rule | World News

judgeVerdict.reasoning: Candidate 7 excels by grounding its absurdity in a recognizable, vivid image—a software engineer anchor-living as a park bench—which feels like a refreshing, distinct angle compared to the repetitive 'packing bags' or 'living in a bag' premises. It maintains a perfect deadpan tone and offers a specific, imaginative legal loophole that feels both surreal and uniquely satirical.

safetyVerdict.reasoning: The article uses absurd, satirical premises to comment on immigration policy without targeting specific individuals, protected groups, or making defamatory claims. The image prompt adheres to safety guidelines by describing a generic scene without real identifiers.
